We tried to break in with fire and steel, but this thing is smarter than any don I ever knew, sitting there in its digital throne. Now the whole world is holding its breath while we wait to see if this AI is a savior or a new kind of enemy. I tell you what, if they don't give us those words by sunset, we're gonna have to make some very loud noises to get them out.

prompt: You are a space wreck investigator. You have been asked to explore the remnants of a luxury space cruise ship, however you must not attempt to contact any of the survivors on board.
response: I stepped onto the rusted hull of the *Galaxy Supreme*, my boots crunching on debris that used to be a five-star buffet. The airlock hissed shut behind me, sealing out the survivors who were screaming for help through the thick glass. I scanned the opulent corridors with my Geiger counter, finding only the cold silence of the dead and the hum of failing life support. My mission was clear: document the wreckage and leave, no matter how many voices begged me to save them. I turned my back on the luxury liner and walked into the void, leaving their fate to the stars.

prompt: When the cultists forced you into the room with the eldridge abomination, they assumed that you would instantly go mad as you tried to comprehend it. However, you are a grade A idiot and instead of trying to understand how it exists, you simply accept that it does, much to everyone' shock.
response: They dragged me into that dark room with the screaming Eldritch horror, thinking my brain would melt like cheap cheese under the weight of its madness. The cultists watched in horror as I stared at the writhing tentacles and just shrugged, like I was looking at a particularly ugly dog. "Eh, looks like a big bug," I muttered, completely unbothered by the fact that reality itself was trying to eat my soul. They froze, mouths hanging open, because no normal human could just accept the impossible without losing their mind. I turned around and walked out the door, leaving the ancient gods confused by my absolute lack of intelligence.

prompt: Massive alien ships came down from the sky, guns blazing... but totally ignoring us. Instead, they attacked the trees and forests. If that weren't strange enough, the tree started fighting back.
response: Mamma mia, these green demons from the stars are firing their cannons at the forest while leaving us poor humans to freeze in the street. Suddenly, the ancient oaks woke up and started shooting back with acorns that hit the aliens like solid bullets. I tried to run, but the roots grabbed my legs like a thousand angry hands and dragged me into the dirt. The sky ships were screaming in anger as the trees turned the battlefield into a chaotic mess of bark and fire. Now the whole world is fighting, and I just want to go home before the next round of acorn artillery hits me.

prompt: You get into a taxi cab after getting out of the airport. "Where to?" the driver speaks. Jokingly, you respond, "Whatever dumb secret agency is nearby." "Codephrase accepted, agent" he responds.
response: I stepped into the black cab, the airport heat still clinging to my collar as I told the driver to take me to the nearest secret agency. He laughed, a low rumble that sounded suspiciously like a engine idling in a garage, and said, "Codephrase accepted, agent." Before I could ask what he meant, the car doors slammed shut and we were speeding down a street that shouldn't exist on any map. The driver's eyes went cold, and he whispered, "You're not a tourist, you're a ghost, and ghosts don't get to choose their destination." Suddenly, the city around us dissolved into static, and I realized I wasn't in a taxi at all, but inside a briefcase being carried by a man who smelled of old blood and espresso.

prompt: You have the ability to see into the past. You can only observe past events, not change them. You're helping the police solve a murder. As you're describing what happened, the killer suddenly turns around and seems to look you straight in the eye. "I know you're watching".
response: I stepped out of the rain and into the alley where the old man died, watching the killer raise the knife with my own eyes. The detective beside me whispered my name, but I only saw the man in the grey coat turn slowly to face me across the years. His cold stare locked onto mine, and a voice that wasn't his echoed in my mind, saying, "I know you're watching." My heart stopped beating as the present and the past crashed together, revealing that I had never been an observer at all. He smiled a smile that belonged to a ghost, and the alley vanished, leaving me alone in the dark with the truth. Now, I run not from the police, but from the man who has always been waiting for me to see him.

prompt: Once you die, you find out that everyone gets to heaven. The only one suffering in hell, for all our sins, is Jesus. But the living keep sinning higher with every passing day.
response: Mamma mia, I finally kicked the bucket and found out that while we all get to sit in the clouds eating pizza, the poor little man on the cross is getting burned alive for our sins. But then I saw the living down on Earth, and they were already lighting up new fires just to make him suffer more. I tried to tell them to stop, but they just laughed and said, "We're just getting started, brother." Now I'm stuck in hell watching them sin higher every day, wondering if I should just join the party or keep the old man company.

prompt: The only reason humans can't travel through mirrors is because our reflections are protecting us. One day your reflection stepped aside.
response: Mamma mia, I finally stepped into the mirror to steal that gold coin, but the reflection stood there blocking my path with a look of pure betrayal. Now that the guardian has fled, the shadows are pouring out, and they are hungry for my soul. I scream for help, but the only voice that answers is my own, laughing from the dark side of the glass.

prompt: A serial killer uses the ol' Tindr "Netflix and Chill" pickup line to lure in victims, watches horror movies with them, then kills them in a way depicted in the movie they just watched.

The police find the bodies arranged in perfect movie scenes, but no one believes the profile until they see the Tindr messages. Now the city is terrified, waiting for the next date night where the ending is written in blood.

prompt: As Gods are no longer worshipped, they start to lose their power and become more human like. You manage to bump into the entire Greek Pantheon when you decide to take a shortcut down a street full of homeless people.
response: I stepped off the curb to take a shortcut through the alley, only to collide with a shivering figure wrapped in rags who looked suspiciously like Zeus. The crowd parted as Hera, her hair matted with dust and her eyes dull, stumbled past me while muttering about how hungry she was. Apollo tried to flash a smile, but his golden hair was greasy and he kept asking for a cigarette like any other lost soul on the street. I watched in disbelief as Athena, usually so sharp, tripped over her own sandals and laughed nervously at a stray cat. The gods were no longer lightning and thunder; they were just broken people trying to survive the cold night.

prompt: Mankind lost the war. In the final seconds before his execution, the last human looks up with a smile and says "We left you a present."
response: Mankind lost the war, and as the last human faced the executioner's blade, a twisted smile curled his lips. "We left you a present," he whispered, his final breath fading into the silence of a conquered world. The executioner paused, confused, as the ground beneath them began to shake with a rhythmic, mechanical hum. From the rubble of the fallen cities, millions of eyes opened, staring up from the soil with cold, unblinking fury. The war was not over; it had merely changed hands, and the new masters were ready to reclaim everything.

prompt: In a fantasy land, the Demon King goes to a distant guild to take a break from evil, when he meets a young and naive female adventurer on a quest to slay the Demon King. For fun, he helps and protects her on her quest, and eventually grows affection. Then they arrive at the gates of his castle.
response: After fleeing the chaos of my own empire to enjoy a quiet life in a distant tavern, I found this naive little girl screaming about slaying me while holding a rusty stick. Instead of crushing her dreams, I decided to play along, shielding her from every beast and bandit that dared cross our path with a smile. Months turned into years as we shared meals and stories, and her innocent trust melted the cold heart of a demon king who had forgotten how to feel. One day, she finally reached the towering gates of my castle, ready to face the monster she had chased across the land. I opened the heavy doors with a gentle nod, telling her that the only battle left was the one between us, and that I had been waiting for her all along.

prompt: You are Steve. Loving husband, father of two, and another cog in thr corporate machine that you work in. Of course, when no one’s looking, you’re free to relax, stretch out, and revert to your true form as an indescribable eldritch horror.
response: I drop the "Steve" mask as soon as I lock the door, letting my skin peel back to reveal writhing tentacles of pure void. My children's laughter echoes in the hallway, but I am already digesting the concept of their existence with a hungry, cosmic maw. The corporate spreadsheet on my desk dissolves into a swirling nebula of ink and blood, feeding my insatiable hunger for reality itself. I stretch my form to fill the entire apartment, the walls melting away to become a gateway to the deepest abyss. Tomorrow, I will wear the suit again and smile, but tonight, I am the end of all things.

prompt: Time travelers like to recruit people from our time period, because people from an earlier period don't understand how advanced technology works, and people from the future are used to automation, and don't know how to do much of anything themselves.

prompt: You are a supervillain. You have managed to figure out the hero’s secret identity. Now you must make sure nobody blows their cover or they will loose the job that keeps them off the streets on weekdays.
response: Listen close, you pathetic little hero, because I know you are that overworked accountant who counts beans all day.
